newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom works on simpler Internet terminal.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom works on simpler Internet terminal.

text.p: French telephone operator France Telecom is working on a simplified terminal for Internet access with several European and North American firms, said Michel Bon, France Telecom's chairman.

The terminal, code-named Minitel-Internet, should "allow users to access both the (French) Minitel service and the Internet in simple and comfortable conditions like those of the Minitel," he told a news conference at a multimedia trade show in Le Mans on Tuesday.

The Minitel, a teletext terminal connected to the telephone network, grew rapidly in France in the 1980s and early 1990s because it was simple to install and use. An offer of a free terminal from France Telecom for several years also helped.
Bon said the method of using the planned Internet terminal should not be very different from the way a Minitel is used currently.
He did not say when the terminal could come to the market.
France Telecom currently offers the basic electronic mail service on Minitel, as well as having its own Internet service provider, Wanadoo.
Its attempts in the mid-1990s to export the Minitel, notably to the United States, were thwarted by the growth of the Internet. WEM/SLA
